title: Our Sun and Its Twin
passage: Our Sun and Its Twin. Some believe we all have a twin somewhere out there, someone almost the same as us in every way. For our Sun, it seems it is no longer the only one of its kind in the universe, as scientists discovered a special star that shines just as brightly. They believe it's our Sun's twin. That's because it's very similar in age, size, shape, motion, and chemistry, and creates about the same amount of heat. The scientists named the star HD 186302, and it's about 184 light-years from Earth. Billions of years ago, both stars were in the same crowded area. Then the power of the Milky Way tore everything to pieces. Now, thanks to science, the twins have found each other again. If we are lucky and Sun 2.0 has a planet the same distance from it as our Earth is from our Sun, then maybe something that we only dreamt of could also be possible: Earth 2.0. The chances may be slim, but scientists are already trying to hunt for signs of planets that belong to HD 186302.
